spec.title: The proof tier after example 286's engine changes: every ignored Rust test in release and every Python test tagged proof
spec.description: Runs lib/tools/test_costs.py run --tier proof. The change behind it touches what nearly every proof-tier test runs, the own checker (lib/src/bmc): String, StringBuilder, stream and regex models, lambdas, String[] inputs, paths merged across heaps of two shapes once more than 1024 have been explored (with a new order in which waiting paths are resumed, and a loop's exit a join), an array of computed size taken within one more than the bound, and a contract applied in place of a model of the same call. The default run passes inline; the values sweep showed that merging heaps from the first path turns a proof by gate hashing into a hard equivalence, which is why it now waits for 1024 paths, so a proof-tier check that explores more than that (the heap and conformance suites) may take longer or run out of time where it did not: this job is where that would show.

resources.notes: past jobs, one test file or test each: heap's tests 3 s to 42 min (up to 61 min at a 1800 s limit), conformance's 11 and 20 min, the benchmark under a minute, each at 1.2 to 1.9 GiB peak; four at a time
